Synopsis:
A cluster of energy companies — Chevron, ENI, KEO Capital and Primavera — are set to sign energy agreements with Venezuela (PDVSA) as early as Wednesday, under a broad Venezuelan oil reform approved in January. Chevron commits $7B+ to more than double crude output to ~600k bpd over five years. KEO Capital secures operatorship of the Petrourdaneta JV with a $350M credit facility. ENI seeks expansion into the Orinoco Belt alongside existing offshore gas and shallow water oil projects. The signings are to be overseen by Venezuela's oil minister and the US Secretary of Energy, signalling high-level political backing on both sides.
